exposure: Intrauterine exposure to hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP)
outcome: Postnatal growth (Z-scores for height and weight)
cohort: The study included 5,144 extremely and very preterm infants (n=1,188 HDP; n=3,956 non-HDP) from a nationwide database, weighing ≤1,500 g and born between 22 and 31 weeks of gestation.
finding: Intrauterine exposure to hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) was associated with accelerated postnatal weight growth in extremely and very preterm infants during early childhood, with no significant sex differences observed.
